decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Gengar, held back as the late Shadow Tag trap (Shadow Ball 2x SE into Metagross, 200 Spe). Lead Incineroar+Kingambit repeats the G1-winning Dark core: Fake Out buys tempo, Kowtow threatens Metagross/Rotom-W, Incineroar is immune to Zen Headbutt. Skarmory is the dedicated Excadrill/Metagross wall (Body Press SE into Excadrill, Sturdy+Leftovers), patching the expected G2 addition. Kingambit stays healthy for the 2v4 close; avoid priority into Farigiraf.
decisions.notebook: Opponent modes: (a) Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind + Mega Metagross/scarf Excadrill offense; (b) Farigiraf+Banette Trick Room (Armor Tail blocks Fake Out/Sucker Punch while Farigiraf is up); (c) Rotom-W burn support. G1 bring: Whimsicott/Banette/Metagross/Rotom-W; Excadrill+Farigiraf stayed home — expect one or both in G2. Confirmed: Incineroar+Kingambit 2v4 closes vs Metagross/Rotom-W; opponent chains Protect to stall double-targets (repeat Protects fail — punish by doubling the partner) and aims WoW at Kingambit. Calcs: Rotom-W Hydro Pump 78-135% to Incineroar (no Protect). Kingambit Kowtow (Black Glasses): 48-89% Rotom-W, 63-108% Mega Metagross. Incineroar Flare Blitz 66-112% Mega Metagross; resisted Blitz 25-46% vs Rotom-W. Mega Gengar (200 Spe) outspeeds Metagross, Shadow Ball 2x SE, Shadow Tag traps; dies to any hit — field only when Banette/Shadow Sneak is gone. Burned Kingambit still walls Metagross. Skarmory: Body Press 2x SE into Excadrill, walls Metagross/Excadrill with Sturdy. G2 team: Incineroar+Kingambit lead, Skarmory+Gengar back. Vs Farigiraf avoid priority, use direct attacks; keep Kingambit healthy vs Excadrill (Sucker Punch neutral).

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Metagross. Whimsicott + Metagross establishes Tailwind while threatening Mega Gengar with super-effective Zen Headbutt; alternatively Moonblast/Ice Punch can deny Noivern’s Tailwind. Rotom-Wash checks Incineroar and Skarmory, while Farigiraf’s Armor Tail protects the endgame from Fake Out and Sucker Punch.

Metagross cannot meaningfully damage either active (Mash/Ice Punch resisted, Zen Headbutt immune), so the only real threat is Tailwind enabling the backline. Fake Out denies Tailwind unless Whimsicott Protects, and Kowtow chunks Metagross 63-108%, forcing it out or into Sucker Punch range next turn. Guaranteed value either way; I keep both mons healthy and scout their switch before committing Skarmory/Gengar.

Burned Kingambit still walls Metagross (its whole set is resisted/immune into him). Skarmory: Body Press 2x SE into Excadrill, walls Metagross/Excadrill with Sturdy. G2 team: Incineroar+Kingambit lead, Skarmory+Gengar back. Vs Farigiraf avoid priority, use direct attacks; keep Kingambit healthy vs Excadrill (Sucker Punch neutral). Encore fails on turn 1 (no prior move) — Fake Out freely denies Tailwind.

decisions.rationale: Pivoting Whimsicott denies the likely Fake Out while Mega Metagross safely scouts the double-Dark pressure. Rotom-Wash immediately threatens Incineroar with Hydro Pump next turn and preserves Whimsicott’s Tailwind for a cleaner board.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 opponent led Incineroar + Kingambit into Whimsicott + Metagross. Preserve Whimsicott for later Tailwind rather than allowing Fake Out to deny it immediately. Mega Metagross is the intended Mega in this mode; use Protect to absorb/scout Dark- and Fire-focused opening pressure while Rotom-Wash pivots in to pressure Incineroar.

decisions.rationale: Metagross-Mega's entire set is resisted or immune into both my actives, so Rotom-Wash is the only real threat. Doubling Dark into its slot KOs through Sitrus Berry on most rolls (combined 84-154%), punishes any switch-in (Banette/Farigiraf take 2x SE, Excadrill takes heavy neutral), and if Rotom Protects we lose nothing since Metagross can't hurt us. Worst case Hydro Pump KOs Incineroar, but Kingambit+Skarmory still wall Metagross for the endgame.
decisions.notebook: Opponent modes: (a) Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind + Mega Metagross/scarf Excadrill offense; (b) Farigiraf+Banette Trick Room (Armor Tail blocks Fake Out/Sucker Punch while Farigiraf is up); (c) Rotom-W burn support. Kingambit Kowtow (Black Glasses): 48-89% Rotom-W, 63-108% Mega Metagross. Incineroar Lariat 36-66% Rotom-W; Flare Blitz 66-112% Mega Metagross. Mega Metagross's whole set is resisted/immune into Incineroar AND Kingambit — it cannot hurt either; ignore it and kill its partners first. Burned Kingambit still walls Metagross. Skarmory: Body Press 2x SE into Excadrill, walls Metagross/Excadrill with Sturdy. Mega Gengar (200 Spe) outspeeds Metagross, Shadow Ball 2x SE, Shadow Tag traps; dies to any hit — field only when Banette/Shadow Sneak is gone. Vs Farigiraf avoid priority, use direct attacks; keep Kingambit healthy vs Excadrill (Sucker Punch neutral). Encore fails on turn 1 — Fake Out freely denies Tailwind.

decisions.rationale: Metagross-Mega cannot safely remain exposed to Kingambit's super-effective Dark attacks, and its repeat Protect is unreliable. Pivoting Farigiraf preserves the intended endgame while Rotom threatens the immediate Incineroar KO; if Incineroar stays in, it cannot also Parting Shot away.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: opponent opened Incineroar + Kingambit, using Fake Out on the Rotom switch and Kowtow Cleave into protected Mega Metagross. Preserve Mega Metagross from Kingambit's Dark pressure; Farigiraf can enter to enable Armor Tail and later Trick Room. Rotom-Wash is the primary immediate Incineroar punish, but Hydro Pump accuracy must be respected.

decisions.rationale: Bring Mega Metagross now: Whimsicott is the stronger remaining speed-control endgame piece and can still support Mega later with Tailwind or punish Protect/Parting Shot lines using Encore. Metagross also avoids immediately exposing Whimsicott to Incineroar and Kingambit’s listed attacking moves.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: opponent opened Incineroar + Kingambit. Incineroar revealed Fake Out, Darkest Lariat, and Sitrus Berry; Kingambit revealed Kowtow Cleave and Black Glasses. Preserve Whimsicott’s Tailwind/Encore utility for the Mega Metagross endgame; Armor Tail prevents priority Sucker Punch but not Kingambit’s Kowtow Cleave.

decisions.rationale: Both foes are harmless: Metagross's whole set is resisted/immune into my Darks, Farigiraf's only attack (Psychic Noise) is immune. Split targets to beat Protect: Kowtow Cleave (never misses, 86-160%) removes Farigiraf and its Armor Tail, unlocking Sucker Punch/Fake Out; Lariat chunks Metagross 47-81% with no recoil risk. If Farigiraf Protects, Metagross still takes the chunk; Trick Room only makes Kingambit faster. Next turn Sucker Punch cleans Metagross; Gengar-Mega/Skarmory handle Whimsicott.
decisions.notebook: Opponent modes: (a) Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind + Mega Metagross/scarf Excadrill offense; (b) Farigiraf+Banette Trick Room (Armor Tail blocks Fake Out/Sucker Punch while Farigiraf is up); (c) Rotom-W burn support. G2 full bring confirmed: Whimsicott/Metagross/Rotom-W/Farigiraf (no Banette/Excadrill). Farigiraf's only attack is Psychic Noise — cannot damage Dark types; it only Trick Rooms/Imprisons/Protects. Tendencies: chains Protect to stall double-targets (punish by splitting onto the partner); aims WoW at Kingambit. Calcs: Kingambit Kowtow (Black Glasses): 86-160% Farigiraf, 63-108% Mega Metagross, 48-89% Rotom-W. Incineroar Lariat: 47-81% Mega Metagross; Flare Blitz 66-112% but recoil danger at low HP. Mega Metagross's whole set is resisted/immune into Incineroar AND Kingambit — ignore it, kill partners first. Whimsicott: Moonblast 2x SE kills low-HP Incineroar; Iron Head (Steel 2x vs Fairy) and Mega Gengar Sludge Bomb (4x SE) delete it. Mega Gengar (200 Spe) outspeeds Metagross, Shadow Ball 2x SE, Shadow Tag traps; dies to any hit. Skarmory Body Press walls Metagross/Excadrill with Sturdy. G3 prep: expect Excadrill/Banette mode; keep Kingambit healthy for Excadrill, Gengar only after Shadow Sneak/Banette is gone.

decisions.rationale: Kingambit is immune/resisted to everything the opponent's active pair can do, so the free slot goes to offense. Mega Gengar (200 Spe) outspeeds Metagross (max 178), traps both with Shadow Tag so Whimsicott can't pivot in, and Shadow Ball + Kowtow Cleave guarantees the Metagross KO even at min rolls. Farigiraf cannot damage Kingambit at all; Skarmory stays as the safe endgame wall for Whimsicott/Excadrill-style cleanup.
decisions.notebook: Opponent modes: (a) Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind + Mega Metagross/scarf Excadrill offense; (b) Farigiraf+Banette Trick Room (Armor Tail blocks Fake Out/Sucker Punch); (c) Rotom-W burn support. G2 bring: Whimsicott/Metagross/Rotom-W/Farigiraf. Farigiraf's only attack is Psychic Noise - cannot damage Dark types. Calcs: Kingambit Kowtow (Black Glasses): 86-160% Farigiraf, 63-108% M-Metagross. Mega Gengar Shadow Ball: 46-98% M-Metagross - combined with Kowtow always KOs. Gengar plan: Mega = 200 Spe outspeeds Metagross, Shadow Tag traps, but dies to any hit (Whimsicott Moonblast, Metagross Zen Headbutt both SE). Kingambit is immune/resisted to Metagross's full set + Farigiraf + Whimsicott Moonblast (0.5x); Iron Head 2x SE deletes Whimsicott. G3 prep: expect Excadrill/Banette mode; keep Kingambit healthy for Excadrill, Gengar only after Shadow Sneak/Banette gone; Skarmory Body Press walls Metagross/Excadrill with Sturdy.

decisions.rationale: Meteor Mash is a guaranteed KO on Incineroar from its shown HP and Metagross is guaranteed faster. Farigiraf Protect denies a possible Kowtow Cleave into its Dark weakness, preserves Armor Tail against later Sucker Punch, and keeps Trick Room available for the endgame. Do not expose Metagross to Flare Blitz by passively Protecting.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: opponent opened Incineroar + Kingambit. Incineroar revealed Fake Out, Darkest Lariat, Sitrus Berry, and is slower than Mega Metagross. Kingambit revealed Kowtow Cleave, Black Glasses, and Protect; Armor Tail blocks its Sucker Punch but not Kowtow. Preserve Whimsicott’s Tailwind/Encore and Farigiraf’s Trick Room/Imprison options for the Mega Metagross endgame.

decisions.rationale: Mega Gengar hits 200 Spe, outspeeding Jolly M-Metagross (max 178), and Shadow Tag traps both foes. Shadow Ball chips Metagross 60-131%; Kowtow KOs Farigiraf (79-177%) and punishes a Metagross Protect. If Gengar trades to Zen Headbutt/Psychic Noise after moving, Kingambit always KOs the chipped Metagross next turn (58-120% vs <=40% left); Kingambit is immune/resisted to both foes' full sets, with Skarmory+Sturdy as backstop. Splitting beats their Protect-stall tendency.

decisions.rationale: Protecting Metagross denies Shadow Ball while Psychic Noise punishes any Gengar attack. Zen Headbutt risks Destiny Bond trading Metagross, whereas this line preserves the key endgame piece even if Gengar Protects or Destiny Bonds and Kingambit removes Farigiraf.

Kingambit revealed Kowtow Cleave, Black Glasses, and Protect; Armor Tail blocks its Sucker Punch but not Kowtow. Gengar’s revealed set includes Shadow Ball, Sludge Bomb, Destiny Bond, and Protect; account for possible Mega Evolution/Shadow Tag. Preserve Whimsicott Tailwind/Encore and Mega Metagross for the endgame.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Sludge Bomb is a guaranteed OHKO on Whimsicott and fires before any non-Tailwind attack (Gengar 200 Spe). Kowtow chips Metagross 63-108%, possible KO. Worst branch (Tailwind -> Zen Headbutt KOes Gengar first) still leaves full-HP Kingambit (immune/resists Metagross's whole set, Sucker Punch +1 ignores Tailwind) plus Sturdy Skarmory (Body Press 2x SE) versus chipped Metagross + Whimsicott, which cannot break either. Every branch wins the game and the series.

decisions.rationale: Metagross cannot safely attack through Sucker Punch and Shadow Ball. Encore forces Kingambit back into its revealed Kowtow Cleave rather than Sucker Punch, while Protect is the only immediate way to deny the double target; its reduced success rate is the necessary risk.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Incineroar revealed Fake Out, Darkest Lariat, Sitrus Berry, and was slower than Mega Metagross. Kingambit revealed Kowtow Cleave, Black Glasses, Protect, and Sucker Punch; it can priority-pick off Mega Metagross once Armor Tail is gone. Gengar revealed Shadow Ball, Sludge Bomb, Destiny Bond, Protect, Mega Evolution, and Heal Block interaction from Psychic Noise. Preserve Whimsicott Tailwind/Encore as speed and move-lock tools; account for Gengar Shadow Ball and Kingambit Sucker Punch jointly when positioning Metagross.

decisions.rationale: 2v1 endgame. Metagross at 8% dies to any hit. Gengar (200 Spe) outspeeds and Shadow Ball KOs; if Metagross attacks Gengar with Zen Headbutt, Kingambit's +1 priority Sucker Punch KOs it first. Only a successful Protect stalls, and it just failed one—repeat next turn if so. No reason to expose Kingambit or waste Destiny Bond.

Protect is the only line that can deny the immediate Sucker Punch/Shadow Ball knockout. Any attack activates Sucker Punch and leaves Metagross unable to act. Zen Headbutt would be the needed Gengar KO if Kingambit ever declines Sucker Punch, but that is unlikely.

Metagross is the opponent's last Pokemon at 8%. Gengar (200 Spe) outspeeds max-178 Metagross and Shadow Ball KOs through anything except Protect; Kowtow Cleave doubles up so a failed Protect still ends it. If Protect succeeds, repeat next turn with worse odds for them. No risk to Gengar since it moves first.

decisions.rationale: Metagross is in range of both Sucker Punch and Shadow Ball, while any attacking move enables Sucker Punch. Protect is the only line that can deny both immediate attacks; it is reduced-rate but preserves the sole possible path through an opposing misplay.

Metagross is the last foe at 8%. Gengar (200 Spe) outspeeds Jolly Metagross (max 178) and Shadow Ball KOs through anything but Protect; Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave is a guaranteed backup KO. Protect is on a 2-streak (~1/9 success), and even if it works neither of us is hurt and we simply repeat next turn. Doubling up ends the game and the series 2-0.

decisions.rationale: Any damaging move exposes Metagross to Kingambit's priority Sucker Punch, while Gengar can also KO with Shadow Ball. The reduced-success Protect is still the only line that can deny both immediate attacks and preserve a possible next-turn opening.

reflections.summary: Won because the team-preview plan was right: the Gengar+Kingambit core hard-countered the opponent's repeated Metagross/Farigiraf/Whimsicott/Rotom mode. reflections.summary: Lost because the Mega Metagross/Farigiraf/Whimsicott plan had no sustainable answer to Mega Gengar plus Kingambit: Gengar pressured Metagross with Shadow Ball while Kingambit removed support and threatened it with Dark attacks. Prankster Encore could not affect Dark-type Kingambit, so Whimsicott did not provide its intended disruption. Mega Metagross was a poor primary win condition into this revealed double-Dark/Ghost pressure core.
reflections.adjustment: For the next game, reconsider bringing or centering Mega Metagross against Gengar plus Kingambit; choose a four and lead that can immediately pressure both rather than relying on Metagross surviving behind Protect. If Whimsicott is brought, use Tailwind or Moonblast pressure instead of planning Prankster Encore into Kingambit.
reflections.notebook: Opponent: Mega Gengar has Shadow Ball, Sludge Bomb, Destiny Bond, Protect, and is a major special attacker into Metagross. Kingambit has Black Glasses, Kowtow Cleave, Protect, and Sucker Punch; Dark-type immunity prevents Prankster Encore from disrupting it. Gengar+Kingambit jointly overwhelm Mega Metagross once support is removed. Future plan: do not make Mega Metagross the primary answer to this pair without immediate double-target pressure and preserved support; Whimsicott's Encore is not a Kingambit answer.
